subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should this TUI request be resolved by documenting the existing pi-tui newline behavior, or should OpenClaw add an owned configurable send/newline keybinding surface?
rationale: Runtime Shift+Enter/Ctrl+J newline insertion is already dependency-backed, but configurable behavior would create a new public TUI config or CLI contract that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Document Existing Behavior First
options.body: Update the TUI guide and /help with Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and the backslash-Enter fallback while deferring configurable keybindings.

options.title: Add Configurable TUI Keybindings
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved TUI config or CLI bridge into pi-tui keybindings with default-compatible tests and docs.

options.title: Close As Dependency-Satisfied
options.body: Treat pi-tui's built-in newline support as enough and explicitly leave docs/help/configurability out of scope.

recommendation.title: Document Existing Behavior First
recommendation.body: Update the TUI guide and /help with Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and the backslash-Enter fallback while deferring configurable keybindings.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across the TUI implementation, docs, and prior issue review.
